first.rationale: We face simultaneous headwinds: competitor pricing pressure on SMB segment, 6% QoQ activation decline, and 4% onboarding completion drop. Memory_73 demonstrates promotional pricing directly addresses price-sensitive SMB acquisition and cuts time-to-first-value—both critical when competitors are undercutting. Memory_31 shows simplification lifts activation. However, promotional pricing offers immediate revenue defense against competitive threat while also supporting activation (via faster time-to-value per memory_73). We verify memory_73 and memory_31 to confirm the interaction between pricing and activation dynamics. This addresses the most acute business threat (competitive displacement) while the mechanism (time-to-first-value improvement) also helps with our secondary activation decline. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is high-value but targets a different segment and won't directly counter SMB price competition. Referral_incentive (memory_57) builds on existing customer base strength but doesn't address new customer acquisition pressure.
